mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: At equal water heights, the wider column has greater bottom pressure.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Equal-height columns of water and oil have equal bottom pressure.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: A taller water column produces lower bottom pressure.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Upper and lower taps supplied by the same overhead tank have equal pressure.

intelligence.enrichment: In a vertical liquid column, pressure at the bottom increases as the height of the liquid column increases; equal heights of the same liquid produce equal pressure even when the columns have different diameters. Raising the water column height increases bottom pressure and produces a larger bulge or stronger stream; changing diameter without changing height does not increase the bottom pressure in the column comparison. The learner predicts bottom or tap pressure from liquid column height, not from the total water amount or pipe diameter. The tap with the most water stored above it always has the strongest stream, even if the water level height is the same.
